title: Norfolk Southern’s Safety Train hosts free Chicago first responder training
body_markdown:
Norfolk Southern’s Safety Train stopped in Chicago Sept. 8–10, giving local first responders from the Chicago Fire Department (CFD) free, hands-on experience responding to rail-related emergencies.


Hosted at Union Pacific’s Global I Yard on Chicago’s Near West Side, the three-day program brought railroad experts and emergency personnel together for hands-on training to strengthen public safety and ensure first responders are prepared to respond effectively in the event of a rail emergency.


The Chicago stop was part of Norfolk Southern’s[Operation Awareness & Response (OAR](https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/commitments/safety/first-responder-training) ) program, a networkwide initiative launched in 2015 to connect first responders with rail-specific training and resources. In 2025, more than 5,800 first responders participated in OAR training through Safety Train stops, fire house visits, and other learning opportunities.


**Hands-on experience**


In total, more than 100 CFD personnel participated in the training at UP Global I, taking part in exercises and drills that replicated real-world emergency scenarios.


**Relationships that strengthen readiness**


Freight rail is the safest way to transport hazardous materials over land, with more than 99.99% of shipments arriving without a release, according to the Association of American Railroads. Because rail incidents can differ from emergencies first responders encounter most often, joint training helps railroad teams and local agencies build a shared understanding of equipment, communications and response priorities before an emergency occurs.


Through OAR, Norfolk Southern continues to invest in practical training, information-sharing and local partnerships that help communities prepare for the unlikely event of a rail emergency. The Chicago training marked the Safety Train’s 12th stop of 2026. Upcoming stops include Frankfort, Ill., Macon, Ga. and S. Charleston, S.C. More information is available at[NorfolkSouthern.com](https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/commitments/safety/first-responder-training/training) .
